newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise on German issuance news.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise on German issuance news.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Friday, cheered by news that Germany did not plan to issue any more 10-year or 30-year debt this year.
"We have seen good foreign interest since early on and that is partly a consequence of the Bundesbank's announcement on Thursday," a dealer said.

At 1100 GMT the benchmark eight percent Danish state bond due 2006 was up half a point from Thursday's 106.69 close to 107.19, in turnover of 3.2 billion crowns. Its December future rose 0.40 point to 106.24 with 479 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.15 point to 84.60.
The crown firmed further, to 3.8407 per mark, from around 3.8417 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany fell to 88 basis points, from 93 around noon yesterday.

The central bank said it sold a total of 16.5 billion crowns of three, six and nine-month treasury bills at its monthly auction, at reduced minimum rates of 3.48, 3.60 and 3.70 percent respectively. --Kenneth Lund, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969651
